edges.description: MRM2 is needed for late assembly of the mitoribosome large subunit independently of its methyltransferase activity, so loss of the protein, not loss of the U1369 methyl mark, is what disrupts assembly.
Severe cerebral atrophy developed in the year after the acute stroke-like episode, on top of the multiple stroke-like lesions seen on early MRI.

nodes.description: Homozygous MRM2 variants have been reported in three families: the missense p.Gly189Arg (c.567G>A) at a residue conserved from E. coli RrmJ to human in the index MELAS-like patient, a donor splice-site variant c.8+1G>T that produces a frameshifted transcript in a subset of mRNAs in a dystonia family, and the missense p.Ala81Val in a family with a neurodevelopmental disorder. Yeast complementation showed that the allele carrying the equivalent of p.Gly189Arg cannot rescue respiration.

nodes.description: Reduced mitochondrial translation causes deficiency of several respiratory chain complexes. In the index patient's muscle complexes I and IV were severely affected. Patient fibroblasts grown in standard medium did not show the defect, which the authors attribute to the tissue specificity of mitochondrial translation disorders.

nodes.description: The 16S rRNA A-loop modified by MRM2 and its neighbour MRM3 is part of the peptidyl transferase centre, and MRM2 acts during late maturation of the mitoribosome large subunit together with the GTPase GTPBP5. Without MRM2 the large subunit assembles aberrantly.

nodes.description: MRM2 is the 2'-O-ribose methyltransferase for uridine U1369 of human 16S mitochondrial rRNA, a residue in the A-loop of the peptidyl transferase centre that contacts aminoacyl-site tRNA. Loss of MRM2 activity removes this modification. Work in MRM2 knockout cells shows that large-subunit assembly does not require the methyltransferase activity, so this node is recorded as a consequence of MRM2 loss with no downstream edge; whether the missing methyl mark itself contributes to disease is not known.
